ORDINANCE NO. 22 OF 2024

AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND THE CODE OF CABOT; DECLARING AN
EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, there has been a recent increase in individuals camping or otherwise
sleeping on public property. The that the health, safety, and welfare of its citizens require the
regulation of camping and sleeping in public spaces; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council hereby finds that camping or otherwise sleeping on
public property is detrimental to the health, safety, and welfare of the citizens of Cabot for each
of the following independent reasons: it can pose real and significant safety hazards to both
those sleeping/camping and to members of the general public, such hazards include but are not
limited to, unsanitary conditions, fire hazards, and environmental degradation; it can block or
otherwise impair the public’s access and use of roads, sidewalks, parks, and other public areas,
these problems are exacerbated when access to these areas are protected by state and federal law;
and it can have a negative effect on local businesses and business owners; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council finds that the City has a significant interest in
maintaining clean, safe, and accessible public spaces for all residents and visitors and it is the
intent of this legislation to ensure the same; and

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS:

SECTION 1: The Code of Cabot is hereby amended to include the provisions as set
forth in Exhibit “A”, attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference.

SECTION 2: The Code changes enacted herein shall not apply to City-owned property
under the sole management and control of the Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission, the
Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission, or other independent commission properly established
under state law unless and until said commission(s) choose to adopt these or similar provisions.
The City Council acknowledges that state law gives said commissions sole authority over the
matters regulated herein for property under their care.

SECTION 3: Any municipal legislation or portion of municipal legislation in conflict

with this Ordinance is hereby repealed to the extent of the conflict.

Section 1. Definitions:

1.

3.

"Public Property" means any public sidewalk, street, alleyway, right-of-way, or
City-owned property.

"Campsite" means any place where bedding, sleeping bag, or other material used
for bedding purposes, or any stove or fire is placed, established, or maintained for
the purpose of maintaining a temporary place to live, whether or not such place
incorporates the use of any tent, lean-to, shack, or any other structure, or any
vehicle or part thereof.

“Camp” means to set up or to remain in or at a camp-site.

Section 2. Sleeping or Camping on Public Property Prohibited:

1.

No person may sleep outdoors on public property at any time as a matter of
individual and public safety. This prohibition includes, but is not limited to, city-
owned structures and parts of structures that are not fully enclosed, such as the
Railyard Pavilion.

No person may camp or occupy a campsite outdoors on public property as a
matter of individual and public safety. This prohibition includes, but is not
limited to, city-owned structures and parts of structures that are not fully
enclosed, such as the Railyard Pavilion.

In addition to any other remedy provided by law, any person found in violation of
this section may be immediately removed from the premises. Such removal is
hereby deemed to be a legitimate governmental! function for the purposes of the
Obstructing Governmental Operations statute under state law. Any person
removed from a campsite or other location where they are sleeping hereunder
must take all personal property with them. Personal property left behind shall be
considered abandoned and may be immediately disposed of by a member of the
Cabot Police Department or other City employee.

Section 3. Penalties:

1.

In addition to any other remedies listed herein, a violation of any of the
prohibitions of any section herein shall be considered a violation of the Code of
Cabot. Upon conviction, a violator shall be sentenced to a fine of up to $100.
Subsequent convictions shall be punished with a fine of up to $500.

RESOLUTION NO. 28 OF 2024
A RESOLUTION DECLARING THE STRUCTURE LOCATED AT 402
SOUTH POLK STREET IN THE CITY OF CABOT TO CONSTITUTE A
PUBLIC NUISANCE AND CONDEMNING SAID STRUCTURE;
PROVIDING A PERIOD OF TIME FOR THE PROPERTY OWNERS TO
ABATE SAID NUISANCE; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the buildings and structures whose location is set forth herein are found to be
dilapidated, unsightly, unsafe, unsanitary, obnoxious, and/or detrimental to the public welfare; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council hereby finds that the condition of such property
constitutes a serious hazard to the City of Cabot, and unless immediate actions are taken to remedy
this situation by removing, razing and abating said nuisance, there is a great likelihood that a threat
is posed to the life, safety, or property of the public. This structure constitutes a serious hazard to
the health and safety of the citizens of Cabot and should therefore be moved or razed for the
purpose of eliminating such hazards.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
OF CABOT ARKANSAS:

SECTION 1: That the City Council hereby declares the buildings, houses and other
structures located at the property identified in Section 2 of this Resolution and owned by David
and Connie MeNair to be dilapidated, unsafe, unsanitary, obnoxious, unfit for human occupancy,
or otherwise detrimental to the life, property, or safety of others. Further details are included in the
attached Exhibit A, incorporated herein by this reference. The City Council further declares that,
because of those conditions, the property is hereby condemned as a public nuisance and is ordered
abated, removed or razed by the owner thereof.

SECTION 2: That the owners of record of 402 South Polk Street, Cabot Arkansas, 72023,
David and Connie McNair, are hereby directed to raze the same or otherwise abate the said
nuisance within thirty (30) days after of a true copy of this Resolution being mailed to the owners
or the owners otherwise being provided notice of this resolution as allowed by law.

SECTION 3: If the aforementioned structures have not been razed and/or removed, or the

nuisances otherwise abated, within the thirty-day time period referenced above in Section 2, the

Council Meeting Minutes for
City of Cabot, Arkansas
508 N. LincoIn
Cabot, AR 72023
September 16, 2024
6:30 pm.

This event was successfully streamed through YouTube. This meeting may be viewed
here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fg66p3_dRMI.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular Meeting of the Cabot City Council at 6:47
pm immediately following the Work Session. Council Member Brandon Hillenburg led the
prayer, and Council Member Corey Spangler led the Pledge of Allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present: Brandon
Hillenburg, James Reid, Matt Webber, Corey Spangler, Stephen Redd, Maggie
Cope, and Ed Long. Ron Waymack was absent. Mayor Kincade, City Attorney Ben
Hooper, and City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom also attended.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

Mr. Redd, seconded by Mr. Reid, motioned to approve the July 15 council meeting
minutes. The motion passed unanimously.

Ms. Cope, seconded by Mr. Hillenburg, motioned to approve the August 19 council
meeting minutes. The motion passed unanimously.

Mr. Webber, seconded by Mr. Redd, motioned to read the legislation by title only.
The motion passed unanimously.

City Council

OLD BUSINESS: ORDINANCE NO. 22 OF 2024 — AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND THE
CODE OF CABOT; DECLARING AND EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES was read
by title only by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Mr. Long motioned to waive the
third reading, seconded by Mr. Webber. The motion passed by a roll call vote of 7-0. Mr.
Reid motioned to adopt, seconded by Mr. Redd. The motion passed by a roll call vote of
5-2. Mr. Hillenburg and Ms. Cope voted no.

RESOLUTION NO. 28 OF 2024 — A RESOLUTION DECLARING THE STRUCTURE
LOCATED AT 402 SOUTH POLK STREET IN THE CITY OF CABOT TO CONSTITUTE A
PUBLIC NUISANCE AND CONDEMNING SAID STRUCTURE; PROVIDING A PERIOD OF
TIME FOR THE PROPERTY OWNERS TO ABATE SAID NUISANCE; AND FOR OTHER
PURPOSES. Mr. Long motioned to permanently remove this item from the agenda,
seconded by Mr. Reid. The motion passed by a roll call vote of 7-0.

NEW BUSINESS: ORDINANCE NO. 23 OF 2024 — AN ORDINANCE TO SET MILLAGE
TAX RATE TO BE COLLECTED IN 2025 FOR THE CITY OF CABOT; AND FOR OTHER

4

PURPOSES was read by title only by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. First reading.
No action.

ORDINANCE NO. 24 OF 2024 — AN ORDINANCE TO PERMIT COUNCIL MEMBERS,
OFFICIALS, AND/OR MUNICIPAL EMPLOYEES TO DO BUSINESS WITH THE CITY OF
CABOT; SPECIFICALLY, LOUIS CIMINO; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES was read by title
only by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Mr. Reid motioned to waive the second and
third readings, seconded by Mr. Redd. The motion passed by a roll call vote of 7-0. Mr.
Webber motioned to adopt, seconded by Mr. Reid. The motion passed by a roll call vote
of 7-0.

ORDINANCE NO. 25 OF 2024 — AN ORDINANCE CREATING, CERTIFYING, AND

Mayor Kincade closed the Council Meeting and opened the Public Hearing at 7:04.

Mayor Kincade explained the hearing is on utilizing Great Strides/Trails for Life grant
funds.

A Parks & Rec staff member spoke in favor of the grant for a hard surface walking trail
at The Grounds. It will be a zero-dollar matching grant of $250,000 if received.

Safety Policy Statement

It is the policy of the City of Cabot to work continually toward improving our
Safety Policy, as well as our safety procedures.

It is the City of Cabot’s intent to provide a safe working environment in all areas,
for all employees. Accident and injuries are prevented by controlling the work
environment and the actions of employees. Therefore, safety will take
precedence over expediency or shortcuts. Every attempt will be made to reduce
the possibility of accident occurrence. Protection of employees, the public, and
City property and operation is paramount. The City of Cabot considers no phase
of the operation more important than the health and safety of the employee.

Employee safety is to be the first consideration in the operation of the business.
Safe practices on the part of the workers must be part of all operations.
Employees must understand their personal responsibility for the prevention of
injuries on and off the job. Accident prevention and efficient production go hand-
in-hand. All injuries can and should be prevented!

The City of Cabot will continue to be guided and motivated by this policy, and
with the cooperation of all employees, will actively pursue a safer working
environment throughout the company.

An accident can be defined as any occurrence that interrupts or interferes with
the orderly progress of the job and usually occurs suddenly and unexpectedly.

Some accidents involve human injury. Accidents arise from a combination of
unsafe acts and unsafe conditions.

II Accident/ Injury Analysis Component

 The Human Resources Department will review and maintain all accident
 investigation reports, hazard reports, incident reports, inspection reports, an
 injury log, and the loss run (from AR Municipal League) on an annual basis, or as
 needed, to determine any trends in accidents or hazards that may be developing.

 The Human Resources Department will recommend corrective actions to be
 taken to prevent recurrence of similar accidents or hazards. The Department
 Heads will be responsible for implementing corrective actions and for tracking the
 status of the corrective actions.

 Documentation of these reviews will be retained by the Human Resources
 Department for a period of 12 months.

III Safety Program Recordkeeping Component

 The Human Resources Department will be responsible for maintaining all
 documentation of training, accident reports, injury logs, hazard reports, incident
 reports, the loss run and any other documentation incidental to the
 implementation of this Health and Safety Plan.

 Blank forms for all safety related training and documentation will be available in
 the Human Resources Department.

 Inspection Records will be kept in the Human Resources Department.

 Safety Meetings/Training Records will be kept in the Human Resources
 Department or by individual Departments.

 Accident Investigation Records will be kept in the Human Resources
 Department.

IV Health and Safety Education and Training Component

 The Human Resources Department and individual Department Heads will be
 responsible for identifying the education and training needs of this facility on an
 annual basis.

 Employees will attend periodic safety meetings/training which will be conducted
 primarily by the individual Department safety officers.

 Safety meetings and safety training will be documented and records will be
 maintained by the Human Resources Department for a period of 24 months or as
 required by law or directives.

 Documentation form (see Appendix A) will include:

 1. Date of training,
 2. Name of trainer,
 3. Subject(s) covered,
 4. Attendance roster with employees’ signatures.

V Safety Inspection Component

 The Human Resources Department will be responsible for conducting and
 documenting safety inspections within the City facilities. Items to be inspected
 are to be documented on the inspection form (see Appendix B).

 Records of all inspections will be kept by the Human Resources Department.

 Employees are responsible for inspecting their work stations for potential hazards
 (see Appendix C). Potential and/or real hazards will be reported in writing to the
 appropriate Department Head.

 The Department Head will recommend corrective actions to be taken.

 Reports will be filed in a log and maintained in the Human Resources
 Department until all discrepancies are corrected or at least 12 months, whichever
 is longer.

 Documentation will include:

 1. Date of inspection,
 2. Name of inspector,
 3. Discrepancies found,
 4. Person responsible for corrections, and
 5. Estimated date of corrections.

 Documentation of these inspections will be kept by the Human Resources
 Department for a period of 12 months.

 City Vehicles will be inspected by the operator prior to use. He or she may utilize
 the form in Appendix D.

VI Accident Investigation Component

 An accident can be defined as any occurrence that interrupts or interferes with
 the orderly progress of the job and usually occurs suddenly and unexpectedly.
 Some accidents involve human injury. Accidents arise from a combination of
 unsafe acts and unsafe conditions.

The intent of an accident investigation should be to determine what basic
condition or act caused the accident so corrective measures can be taken to
prevent reoccurrence and not to identify the guilty party.

Accidents should be investigated as soon as possible. The sooner the
information is gathered, the more accurate the facts will be.

Accident Investigation Procedures:

1) Investigations are required on all accidents, which may include those
 “near misses” not producing injuries. “Near misses” are reviewed to
 determine if a recurring hazard exists. Therefore, they must be thoroughly
 investigated and reported. Accidents that do not produce injury have
 probably produced other job hindrances, such as delays, damaged
 material, damaged equipment, etc.

2) All accidents are to be investigated and documented by the Human
 Resources Department of the employee involved. Investigations will be
 conducted as soon as possible.

3) All incident reports, hazard reports, accident investigation reports and
 inspection checklists will be reviewed by City of Cabot management to
 determine if trends are occurring.

4) The steps for a thorough and effective investigation may include:

 1. Interview the employee(s) involved, if possible, to evaluate the
 situation and potential liability.
 2. Have the involved employee(s) step through the sequence of
 events of the accident.
 3. Locate, interview and get statements from any witnesses.
 4. Gather facts about the investigation (who, what, where, how, why).
 5. Evaluate any evidence found at the scene and reconstruct events.
 6. Take pictures or draw diagrams of the accident scene. Don’t rely on
 memory - accident scenes change.
 7. Do not disturb the accident scene until you are satisfied with the
 investigation.
 8. Before leaving the scene of the accident, warn, protect and/or
 repair any exposure areas to prevent another accident from
 occurring.
 9. Re-interview the involved employee(s) or witnesses, if necessary.
 10. Prepare a written detailed report before leaving for the day.
 11. Recommend corrective actions.
 12. Follow-up on the recommendations to ensure the corrective actions
 have been implemented.

 13. Double-check the corrective action(s) to ensure they are effective.

 5) Once the investigation is completed, it must be directed to the Human
 Resources Department and Department Head for review.

 6) Each person in the review process is responsible for assuring thorough
 investigations and following up on corrective action(s) to make sure it is
 (they are) effective.

 7) Written accident investigation reports (see Appendix E) will be filed in the
 Human Resources Department where they are available for review. The accident
 investigation process is documented by the Human Resources Department and
 will be retained for a period of 24 months or as required by law.

VII Health and Safety Plan Review

 The Human Resources Department and Department Heads will review the Health and
 Safety Plan on an annual basis.

 This review will be to determine if all areas of exposure are addressed in the Health
 and Safety Plan. Any new hazards identified during the review will be included in the
 Health and Safety Plan and employees will receive immediate training when required.

 Annual reviews will be documented (See Appendix F) showing date of review and
 any new areas of exposure identified. Documentation will be maintained by the
 Human Resources Department.

Safety Policy Statement

It is the policy of the City of Cabot to work continually toward improving our
Safety Policy, as well as our safety procedures.

It is the City of Cabot’s intent to provide a safe working environment in all areas,
for all employees. Accident and injuries are prevented by controlling the work
environment and the actions of employees. Therefore, safety will take
precedence over expediency or shortcuts. Every attempt will be made to reduce
the possibility of accident occurrence. Protection of employees, the public, and
City property and operation is paramount. The City of Cabot considers no phase
of the operation more important than the health and safety of the employee.

Employee safety is to be the first consideration in the operation of the business.
Safe practices on the part of the workers must be part of all operations.
Employees must understand their personal responsibility for the prevention of
injuries on and off the job. Accident prevention and efficient production go hand-
in-hand. All injuries can and should be prevented!

The City of Cabot will continue to be guided and motivated by this policy, and
with the cooperation of all employees, will actively pursue a safer working
environment throughout the company.

Safety Policy Statement

It is the policy of the City of Cabot to work continually toward improving our
Safety Policy, as well as our safety procedures.

It is the City of Cabot’s intent to provide a safe working environment in all areas,
for all employees. Accident and injuries are prevented by controlling the work
environment and the actions of employees. Therefore, safety will take
precedence over expediency or shortcuts. Every attempt will be made to reduce
the possibility of accident occurrence. Protection of employees, the public, and
City property and operation is paramount. The City of Cabot considers no phase
of the operation more important than the health and safety of the employee.

Employee safety is to be the first consideration in the operation of the business.
Safe practices on the part of the workers must be part of all operations.
Employees must understand their personal responsibility for the prevention of
injuries on and off the job. Accident prevention and efficient production go hand-
in-hand. All injuries can and should be prevented!

The City of Cabot will continue to be guided and motivated by this policy, and
with the cooperation of all employees, will actively pursue a safer working
environment throughout the company.

The Human Resources Department will be the primary person responsible for the
implementation and enforcement of the City of Cabot Safety Policy.

Additionally, the Human Resources Department or individual Department safety
officers will be responsible for all documentation and records developed as a
result of safety training, meetings, accident investigations and hazard reports
required by this plan.

Accident Investigation Component
An accident can be defined as any occurrence that interrupts or interferes with
the orderly progress of the job and usually occurs suddenly and unexpectedly.

Some accidents involve human injury. Accidents arise from a combination of
unsafe acts and unsafe conditions.

The intent of an accident investigation should be to determine what basic
condition or act caused the accident so corrective measures can be taken to
prevent reoccurrence and not to identify the guilty party.

Accidents should be investigated as soon as possible. The sooner the
information is gathered, the more accurate the facts will be.

Investigations are required on all accidents, which may include those
“near misses” not producing injuries. “Near misses” are reviewed to
determine if a recurring hazard exists. Therefore, they must be thoroughly
investigated and reported. Accidents that do not produce injury have
probably produced other job hindrances, such as delays, damaged
material, damaged equipment, etc.

All accidents are to be investigated and documented by the Human
Resources Department of the employee involved. Investigations will be
conducted as soon as possible.

All incident reports, hazard reports, accident investigation reports and
inspection checklists will be reviewed by City of Cabot management to
determine if trends are occurring.

The steps for a thorough and effective investigation may include:

1. Interview the employee(s) involved, if possible, to evaluate the

situation and potential liability.

Have the involved employee(s) step through the sequence of

events of the accident.

Locate, interview and get statements from any witnesses.

Gather facts about the investigation (who, what, where, how, why).

Evaluate any evidence found at the scene and reconstruct events.

Take pictures or draw diagrams of the accident scene. Don’t rely on

memory - accident scenes change.

Do not disturb the accident scene until you are satisfied with the

investigation.

public to comment.

meetings and facilitating the livestreams; issues that arise on the part of the website or
social media company hosting the livestream; or other circumstances which would make

Section 1 may be temporarily halted but shall be resumed after the issue or issues in

Safety Policy Statement

It is the policy of the City of Cabot to work continually toward improving our
Safety Policy, as well as our safety procedures.

It is the City of Cabot’s intent to provide a safe working environment in all areas,
for all employees. Accident and injuries are prevented by controlling the work
environment and the actions of employees. Therefore, safety will take
precedence over expediency or shortcuts. Every attempt will be made to reduce
the possibility of accident occurrence. Protection of employees, the public, and
City property and operation is paramount. The City of Cabot considers no phase
of the operation more important than the health and safety of the employee.

Employee safety is to be the first consideration in the operation of the business.
Safe practices on the part of the workers must be part of all operations.
Employees must understand their personal responsibility for the prevention of
injuries on and off the job. Accident prevention and efficient production go hand-
in-hand. All injuries can and should be prevented!

The City of Cabot will continue to be guided and motivated by this policy, and
with the cooperation of all employees, will actively pursue a safer working
environment throughout the company.

The Human Resources Department will be the primary person responsible for the
implementation and enforcement of the City of Cabot Safety Policy.

Additionally, the Human Resources Department or individual Department safety
officers will be responsible for all documentation and records developed as a
result of safety training, meetings, accident investigations and hazard reports
required by this plan.

An accident can be defined as any occurrence that interrupts or interferes with
the orderly progress of the job and usually occurs suddenly and unexpectedly.

Some accidents involve human injury. Accidents arise from a combination of
unsafe acts and unsafe conditions.

condition or act caused the accident so corrective measures can be taken to
prevent reoccurrence and not to identify the guilty party.

Accidents should be investigated as soon as possible. The sooner the

which it will operate a veterinarian college and other related uses. The City and Lyon will also

cost and no-cost, to the Cabot community; and

WHEREAS, The Cabot City Council finds that the agreement and other actions contemplated
herein constitute clear and obvious public purposes and are being undertaken by the City primarily for the
public benefit. These public purposes include, but are not limited to: furthering access to veterinary
education; furthering local access to veterinary care, especially considering Arkansas’s very low per-
capita rating in that area; these facilities will significantly expand the City’s capacity to provide animal
care services to the surrounding area; the overall positive economic impact to the community and the
many jobs created over time; and

dedicated to pay the City’s lease payments for the property at issue. The funds received from the sublease
will be more than sufficient to pay for the City’s lease. As such, tax revenues will not be used in making
the City’s lease payments discussed herein; and

WHEREAS, the lease and sublease at issue will contain provisions that allow the Cabot City
Council, at any time and for any reason, to decline to further appropriate lease payments for the City’s
lease. As such, the Cabot City Council will have the ultimate authority over the continuation or
termination of the lease and sublease in question; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council is empowered to authorize the lease and sublease referenced
herein under A.C.A. 14-54-302. The City Council finds that the lease and sublease referenced herein are
lease contracts as set forth in that statute and that the City Council therefore has the statutory authority to
authorize the lease and sublease through a majority vote to approve this Resolution; and

consistent with the attached Exhibit A, incorporated herein by this reference, and the City Council
recognizes that as a result of the complex lease negotiation process at issue some changes may still be

RESOLUTION NO. 58 OF 2024

A RESOLUTION TO APPROPRIATE AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT
FUNDS; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA), which was signed into law in
March 2021, provides fiscal recovery funds to local governments; and

WHEREAS, ARPA provides support to local governments in responding to the impact
of COVID-19 and in addressing the economy; and

WHEREAS, ARPA created several eligible uses of the funding, including the ability of
awarded cities and towns to address the issue of lost revenue; and

WHEREAS, the United States Department of Treasury on January 6, 2022, issued a
Final Rule regarding the use of ARPA funds; and

WHEREAS, the Final Rule permits cities and towns to utilize one of the statutorily
eligible uses of the funds as “lost revenue or revenue replacement: up to a standard allowance
of $10,000,000 or the total amount of a city’s grant award, whichever is less; and

WHEREAS, the total grant award amount for the City of Cabot is less than $10,000,000;
and

WHEREAS, the Final Rule permits cities and towns to utilize “lost revenue or revenue
replacement” for any government service; and

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: The City Council hereby appropriates $449,450 of the City’s remaining
ARPA funds for the costs of the 2024 salary expenses for non-elected city employees beginning
on January 1, 2024, or for any other permitted expense, and running until the amount is
expended. The funds were originally disbursed from the general operating fund of the City.
This adjustment reduces the 2024 general fund salary expense by $449,450 and increases the
use of the remaining ARPA funds by the same amount.

SECTION 2: The City Council hereby appropriates $570,000 of the City’s remaining

RESOLUTION 62 OF 2024

A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND CITY CLERK~TREASURER
TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH AXON ENTERPRISE, INC.; TO WAIVE
THE COMPETITIVE BIDDING REQUIREMENTS IN ORDER TO ENTER INTO SAID
AGREEMENT; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the Cabot Police Department is in need of five in-car video cameras;
and

WHEREAS, the Police Department’s existing in-car video cameras and related
equipment are primarily Axon branded. It is strongly preferable for the new cameras and related
equipment to also be Axon branded in order for the best and smoothest integration with Police
Department’s personnel and current equipment. The optimal working conditions of the Police
Department’s equipment are of very high importance and direct benefit to the health, safety, and
welfare of the public; and

WHEREAS, Ark. Code Ann § 14-58-303 et al., provides that the governing body may
waive the requirement of competitive bidding in situations where the procedure is deemed not to
be feasible or practical. While there are other providers of in-car video cameras, Axon is the
only licensed provider of the needed equipment that meets all specifications sought by the Police
Department and that would facilitate the best integration with the Department’s current
equipment infrastructure to ensure there is no detrimental impact to the health, safety, and
welfare of the public. As such competitive bidding in this matter is deemed to be neither feasible
nor practical and the requirements of competitive bidding are hereby waived; and

WHEREAS, the in-car cameras in question will be paid for primarily with grant funds
received by the Cabot Police Department from the State of Arkansas; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council supports the Police Department in its purchase of
new in-car video cameras and related equipment from Axon and recognizes that it is the only
licensed source of the equipment that would meet all of the Police Department’s needs, details,
and specifications.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized to enter
into an Agreement with Axon Enterprise, Inc. for the purchase of in-car video cameras and
related equipment and services for the Cabot Police Department. The agreement is
authorized to be in the total amount of $79,785.88 and is to be consistent with Exhibit A,

attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference.
